ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the attached figure there is quadrilateral ABCD, A is at the lower left, B is above and slightly to the left, C is at the upper right, and D is at the lower right. Line segments AC and BD intersect at point T. The double tick marks in the figure are marked on AB and AD, indicating AB = AD; the single tick marks are marked on BC and CD, indicating BC = CD. Therefore ABCD is a kite with AC as the axis-of-symmetry diagonal. Then reason: in a kite, the axis-of-symmetry diagonal perpendicularly bisects the other diagonal BD, so T is the midpoint of BD, and AC ⟂ BD. Given BT = 5, therefore TD = 5; given TC = 8. Thus triangle CTD is a right triangle, with the two right-angle sides CT = 8 and TD = 5, so CD = sqrt(8^2 + 5^2) = sqrt(64 + 25) = sqrt(89).

method.method_draft: From the image, note AB = AD by the double tick marks, BC = CD by the single tick marks, AC is shared, and T lies at the intersection of AC and BD. From the text, take BT = 5 and TC = 8. First prove triangle ABC congruent to triangle ADC by SSS, so AC bisects angle BCD and angle BCT equals angle TCD. Then compare triangles BCT and DCT: BC = CD, CT is common, and the included angles at C are equal, so triangle BCT congruent to triangle DCT by SAS. Hence BT = DT = 5 and angles BTC and CTD are equal. Since B, T, D are collinear, these equal adjacent angles form a straight line, so each is 90 degrees. Therefore triangle CTD is right, and CD = sqrt(CT^2 + DT^2) = sqrt(8^2 + 5^2) = sqrt(89).
